notes: Independently audited all 14 discovery/diamond economics candidates against current official journal, publisher, society or official submission-portal material. Each patch supplies the complete replacement route and a record-specific audit note. This is documentary fee verification, not manuscript acceptance or human scientific review.

Final route fee classifications: 11 verified_free and 3 needs_verification. The verified_free count includes Economics and Business Letters only as a fee policy: discovery submission_status=closed must remain visible and it must not be shown as a currently open opportunity.

Material corrections: Swiss Journal of Economics and Statistics upgraded after the owning society explicitly confirmed free submissions worldwide; JCE demoted because its prospective OUP 2027 fee policy is linked to a staged portal that prohibits live submissions; Public Sector Economics publication_fee corrected to unknown.

JCE prospective OUP no-fee standard licensing is not evidence for any legacy Elsevier submission workflow. OUP author-guideline requests timed out and the Elsevier guide was blocked; no legacy fee amount was imported from secondary sources.

Ordinary fee-free routes exclude optional immediate OA, optional print colour/offprints and author services. Institutional agreements and selective waivers were not used to call a route verified_free. No compulsory journal membership or conference attendance was identified for the verified routes.

AI restrictions and manuscript limits are preserved as operational conditions where observed; fee-free status does not mean a manuscript using Agentic-Powered-Research automatically satisfies the journal’s author-AI policy.
No accounts created, venues contacted, manuscripts submitted, external messages sent or remote repository writes performed. Only the assigned economics fee file was written.
